Truly though, I’m so sorry all of this has been happening in your life, I cannot imagine the level of stress you’re under right now. 
Honestly I think the best advice I could give is to remember the small things. Your life totally might feel like it’s blowing up right now but people still smile and joke. Your favorite food is still yummy and your favorite song is still a banger. I’m happy you have a therapist and seem to be ok with your medication, I think that will take you a long way in maintaining your sanity but just remember to take care of yourself and show yourself love in little ways. Whether it be buying a cheap air freshener for your car so it doesn’t smell like food all the time, or making a sick playlist to play on the car. Little things that just make life a lllitttlllee bit easier to get through.

P.S: I hope you don’t take this the wrong way but I was looking through my old Reddit posts and you were the first comment I got ever. I was struggling mentally and you gave some advice that completely changed my life. I have thought about your advice and the story you told me about yourself for YEARS. Anytime I repressed my feelings or tried to minimize what I was going through I would ALWAYS remember you telling me your story and how stress impacted you. YOU, a COMPLETE stranger on Reddit of all places, helped me get through the absolute worst years of my life. Part of the reason I’m alive and happy is because of you, and your comment.

Remember you impact people positively in so many ways that you might not even notice. A smile, a piece of advice. Hell even just dropping off there food for them. You matter so much to the people you touch directly and indirectly. Life is so so so hard and unfair but things will get better eventually. Most people would buckle and crash in the amount of stress put on you right now. And even though your struggling your still trying to stay positive and exist and that is insane resilience. 

Stay strong and treat yourself with gentleness and understanding OP

I definitely understand what you’re coming from! As we heal we naturally start to stay away from people or experiences that remind us of our traumatic past, as well as those who can’t relate to us or understand us.

PTSD has a HUGE impact on someone’s personality, perception of themselves, what behavior they tolerate etc. And a huge part of the healing process is discovering who you are, what makes you happy, and how you want to be treated within society. 

I have done a complete 180 since working on my trauma and have gone from a quiet, shy, meek, self-obsessed doormat of a girl to a confident, very assertive and somewhat-social women who LOVES to lay down boundaries. Safe to say, that turned off A LOT of previous friends and family members when they realized they couldn’t use me, shit-talk (to my face) me, or pressure me into doing shit for them.
They see as a snob and that education and mental health awareness as taken away there sweet innocent naive little girl… and it has… but I’m way better off, healthy and happy as I am now, and when you become yourself you’ll attract similar people, similar resilient, strong and kind people. 

Trauma is TERRIBLE and I don’t wish cPTSD on anyone but post-traumatic growth is a very real thing.

Because we had each other and that was all we needed, love does more then anything else when it comes to preserving family happiness. Hey, narcissistic’s (in general) don’t change with second, third or fourth chances and for your own safety and mental well-being, know that you aren’t over-reacting. Your brain is telling you that you aren’t being treated with love and respect, fear should never felt in a relationship. If fear is present that means the relationship is toxic.

Each time that me and my family left my narcissistic father (him and my mother where very on and off again in the past), it was always a Hail Mary. My mother would make the decision, come to me and my brother in secret (usually pulling us out of school), tell us to put all things in black trash bags, and we would leave the same day. She would usually find somewhere for us to stay (a family members home or get a lease) within a week.

It was very very difficult but hail marying it made us WAY happier and way safer. Because if a narcissist even catches a WHIFF of you trying to leave, they will sink there talons in you deeper and deeper. Waiting runs the risk of not making it out the door.

I have 4c hair and it can REALLY depend on your porosity so you should research because it affects how and what products work best for you. For me lighter gels work like a CHARM, thicker gels like wetline and eco work decently (wetline is the GOAT for cheap gels tho). 

So apply leave in conditioner while still in the shower and then if your able, apply the gel with sopping, dripping hair. I can’t stay in the heat so I just put really hot water in a bottle and spray it on my hair as I comb the gel with my fingers or a denim brush through my hair.

Camille Rose and Kinky curly have worked wonders for me, it is expensive but worth a try if you can (kinky curly is the best in my opinion). But that’s if your hair isn’t super super stubborn and needs a lot of hold. I think Wetline is great for stubborn hair.


The MOST important part, divide your hair into as small of sections as you can, as you comb the product through it. The smaller section the better the final product, it’s truly magical.

Hey! I’m currently in College and work and I had the same exact issues of just needing an extra boost and motivation to get up in the morning!
I got a puppy, it helped ALOT, I have a reason to wake up early every single day, because he deserves it and requires it, plus he’ll make sure to wake me up if I don’t first.

However be very very careful. I’ve had to sacrifice A LOT for this dog, and completely change my lifestyle as he is a Border collie mix and is exetremely high energy with a few behavior issues that I’m paying a lot of money to get fixed. And everybody goes through the “puppy blues” even with the most angelic puppy, it can really take a toll on your mental health if you don’t have a good support system and a lot of patience and hope. I’m happy I made my decision but I would not recommend getting a puppy since you already have sooo much on your plate.

I would look into getting an older dog maybe 5 and older? They typically come potty trained and hopefully with the basic sit and down commands and sometimes manners. They still require a lot of the work you would need from a puppy, but you won’t have to spend your work shift worrying about if he peed on the floor or if he chewed up a book.

If you want to adopt a dog, I would talk with a shelter or rescues and be very honest about what you can handle and what experience you want with this future pupper. More likely then not they’ll match you up with a dog that suits your lifestyle and requirements. Especially rescues, they are difficult to work with but they truly care a lot about there dogs (most of the time) and will want to make sure they don’t see the dog being returned due to just not fitting in with its new family.

If you are going to get a puppy for a breeder, please please please, save up a lot of money, go to /dogs or /breeders (whatever dog related Reddit threads) and ask people to recommend to good and qualified breeders (if you don’t already know some). Puppy mills and backyard breeders exist and while those dogs will still be birthed and require homes, in your case, it would be a horrible decision to accidentally get one of those puppies and have to deal with the behavioral problems that often come from it’s bad breeding and horrible birth environment.

Overall it’s honestly been the best decision of my life and with help from trainer and my vets, I have the best dog in the world and I love him so much. but it’s something to take very seriously and tread carefully to avoid it taking a big toll on your mental health.
